clue.text: Writer of prose can start to turn verse out

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
when something is put out of order its parts are disturbed and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of turn
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prose writer who can make poetry turn out well.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'turn verse out' as producing poetry, but 'out' rearranges CAN, T and VERSE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Miguel de Cervantes wrote Don Quixote, the famous Spanish novel, so he is a celebrated author of prose fiction.

clue.text: Baddy captured by American agency’s chirpy types

indicators.note: something captured is held inside its captor, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency, plus the possessive S
a cad is a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A villain caught by the CIA, whose agents turn out to be talkative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chirpy' sounds like cheerful spies, but it is meant literally: insects that chirp.
explanation.definitionFit: Cicadas are insects famous for the loud chirping or buzzing noise the males produce in summer.

clue.text: Bishop into something radical, mostly very cold and inhuman

indicators.note: this preposition means entering, so one piece is placed within another
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
a root is the radical source of something; radical comes from Latin for root
ICY with its last letter removed

explanation.surface: A churchman caught up in some radical scheme, chilly and lacking humanity.
explanation.walkthrough: A word meaning very cold loses its final letter to give IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something robotic behaves mechanically, without human feeling or warmth, like a machine.

clue.text: Be got hold of by a merchant working in reception area

indicators.note: letters that are working are set in motion and moved about into a new order
something got hold of is gripped inside whatever holds it

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone being collared by a trader busy in a lobby.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled word takes the two-letter verb inside just before its own final letter, rather than around it.
explanation.definitionFit: An antechamber is a small room leading into a larger one, where visitors wait to be received.

clue.text: Sporting contest – time for Jack to travel

indicators.note: one thing given for another is swapped in to replace it

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
J is the abbreviation for jack in cards
to journey is to travel

explanation.surface: A sports fixture where it is time for a player called Jack to set off.
explanation.walkthrough: JOURNEY has its J replaced by T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourney is a tournament, originally a medieval jousting competition between knights.

clue.text: Curse of firm limited in growth

indicators.note: something limited in is confined within bounds, so it sits inside another piece

blocks.note: a surge is a sudden growth or rise
CO is short for company

explanation.surface: A business blighted by being restricted in how much it can expand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limited' suggests a limited company, but here it is the instruction to put one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a cause of great suffering or affliction, a plague or bane, much like a curse.

clue.text: Problem has engineers attending vehicle

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A breakdown requiring mechanics to come out to a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: RE for the Royal Engineers is a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a puzzle in which pictures and symbols stand for words, a kind of problem to solve.

clue.text: Port imbibed by patriot

indicators.note: what is imbibed is swallowed and sits inside the drinker, so the letters lie within a word

blocks.note: the middle letters of this word

explanation.surface: A glass of port drunk by a loyal patriot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the fortified wine, given 'imbibed', but it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rio de Janeiro, usually shortened to Rio, is a major Brazilian seaport city on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Country woman given education in statistics group

indicators.note: a thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: in statistics a bin is one of the intervals data are grouped into, as in a histogram
Educating Rita is Willy Russell's play about a woman given a university education

explanation.surface: A country girl getting schooling as part of a statistics team.
explanation.walkthrough: Educating Rita, a British play and film, is about a hairdresser studying with the Open University.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain is the island nation of England, Scotland and Wales, commonly used for the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Poet not to lounge?

blocks.note: surface reading: a writer of verse who is told not to laze about
setter's reading: the opposite of slouching is to keep a good, upright posture, which splits into two short words

explanation.walkthrough: The poet's surname, read as two words, is advice against lounging: keep upright posture.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Sitwell was an English modernist poet, sister of the writers Osbert and Sacheverell Sitwell.

clue.text: Measure copper coin

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a bit is a small coin, as in a threepenny bit

explanation.surface: Weighing out a copper coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper coin' reads as one thing, a penny, but splits into two pieces; a threepenny bit was an old British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A cubit is an ancient unit of length based on the forearm, from elbow to fingertip.

clue.text: Our unusual day-to-day record is beginning to trouble medical expert

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal form, so the letters take a different order
the beginning of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a log is a daily record, as kept on a ship
taken as written
first letter of trouble

explanation.surface: Our strange diary of daily symptoms is starting to worry a specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: Only OUR is rearranged; the rest follows in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: A urologist is a doctor specialising in the urinary tract and male reproductive organs.

clue.text: Point made by idiot, learner expelled

indicators.note: someone expelled is thrown out, so that letter leaves the word

blocks.note: a dolt is a stupid person
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A fool makes a remark after a student is thrown out of class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point made' looks like an argument in a debate, but the point is a small mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A dot is a small round mark or spot, a point such as a full stop or decimal point.

clue.text: Secret agent put out in prominent position

indicators.note: to be put out is to be disturbed or thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A spy is exposed by being placed somewhere very conspicuous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' sounds like a spy being sent on a mission or blown, but it signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking centre stage means occupying the most noticeable spot, literally the middle of a theatre's platform.

clue.text: Maybe like things put into boxes or chests I made specially

definitions.text: Maybe like things put into boxes

indicators.note: something done specially is fashioned in a particular new way, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Packing items into boxes or into some chests a carpenter crafted to order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' and 'chests' make one picture of storage, but the chests are just letters; the boxes are those of a diagram or chart.
explanation.definitionFit: Schematised information is arranged into a diagram or scheme, often with items set out in labelled boxes.

clue.text: Office worker about to be dismissed as member of religious group

indicators.note: someone dismissed is sent away, so those letters leave the word

blocks.note: a secretary works in an office
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A clerk about to be sacked for belonging to a cult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to be dismissed' reads as imminent sacking; 'about' is in fact the letters RE to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: A sectary is an old word for a sectarian, a member or zealous adherent of a particular sect.

clue.text: New hotel bringing in a new intoxicant

indicators.note: bringing something in puts it inside, so one piece is held within another
making something new means remaking it, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A newly opened hotel stocking a novel kind of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'new's do different jobs: the first rearranges, the second is just N.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethanol is the alcohol in beer, wine and spirits, the chemical that makes drinkers drunk.

clue.text: Examined excellent item of furniture

blocks.note: plum means choice or excellent, as in a plum job
a bed is an item of furniture

explanation.surface: Inspecting a fine piece of furniture in an antiques shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plumbed' looks like pipework, but here it means probed deeply, as in plumbing the depths.
explanation.definitionFit: To plumb something is to explore or investigate it thoroughly, originally by measuring depth with a weighted line.

clue.text: Fish old fellow catches quietly in Italian river

indicators.note: whatever catches something holds it inside
placed in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
O is the abbreviation for old
a fellow is a man
p is piano, the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: An elderly man quietly landing a fish from a river in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the fellow catches the quiet letter, then old plus fellow together go into the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The pompano is a food fish of the jack family, found in warm Atlantic waters.

clue.text: Story told originally in a French book about a Moabite woman

indicators.note: the original part of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept
placed in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: un is French for a
first letter of told
the Book of Ruth in the Bible tells of Ruth, a woman from Moab

explanation.surface: A tale first told in a French book about a woman from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Story' looks like a narrative, but here it is the childish sense: a fib.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling stories is a mild way of saying telling lies, so a story can be a falsehood.

clue.text: Nobody was such a writer

blocks.note: surface reading: no person at all wrote in this way
setter's reading: the Nobody is Charles Pooter of the Grossmiths' comic novel The Diary of a Nobody

explanation.walkthrough: The Diary of a Nobody is an 1892 English comic novel by George and Weedon Grossmith, told as the journal of a suburban clerk.
explanation.definitionFit: A diarist is someone who keeps a daily journal recording personal events and thoughts.

clue.text: What’s exciting for male? It’s to do with what mini reveals

definitions.text: to do with what mini reveals

indicators.note: to excite is to stir up, so the letters are agitated into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Men find a short skirt exciting because of what it shows.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cheeky: a miniskirt shows the thighs, and the thigh bone is the femur.
explanation.definitionFit: Femoral means relating to the thigh or femur, the part of the leg a short skirt leaves on view.

clue.text: Receiver gets hold of excellent glazed earthenware

indicators.note: getting hold of something means grasping it inside

blocks.note: a fence is a receiver of stolen goods
A1 means excellent, with the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A dealer acquires some fine glazed pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receiver' suggests a radio or phone, but it is a criminal handler of stolen property.
explanation.definitionFit: Faience is tin-glazed decorated pottery, named after the Italian town of Faenza.

clue.text: Hermit with cunning plan to eat half a cake

indicators.note: taking only half of something means the rest is cut away
what is eaten goes inside the eater

blocks.note: a ruse is a cunning trick
the first half of eclair, a cream cake

explanation.surface: A hermit scheming to get his hands on part of a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: The cake has to be one with an even number of letters to halve: the six-letter eclair.
explanation.definitionFit: A recluse lives in seclusion, avoiding other people, just as a hermit withdraws from society.

clue.text: Shining, keen to hide slightest bit of blackness

indicators.note: the smallest bit of a word is its first letter alone
to hide something is to cover it up inside

blocks.note: to keen is to wail in grief, to lament
first letter of blackness

explanation.surface: Bright and eager to conceal any trace of darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like eager, but it is the verb meaning to wail for the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambent describes light that glows softly or flickers over a surface, so it means gently shining.

clue.text: Mum, one of the celebs who values goods above godliness?

definitions.note: a relative clause; with 'one' it describes a person, the noun answer

blocks.note: mater is Latin for mother, old public-school slang for mum
I is the Roman numeral one
the A-list is the top rank of celebrities

explanation.surface: A mother who is a celebrity and prizes possessions over piety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' does double duty in the surface but gives only I in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A materialist cares chiefly about possessions and physical comfort rather than spiritual matters.

clue.text: River settlement not quiet

indicators.note: saying something is not there means it is taken away

blocks.note: a camp is a settlement
p is piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: A noisy village by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cam is the river that flows through Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cam is a river in eastern England, the one punted along beside Cambridge colleges.

clue.text: Grown-up, one getting on, receiving a fan’s fawning

indicators.note: whatever receives something takes it inside

blocks.note: an adult is a grown-up
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly adult being flattered by an admirer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One getting on' looks like an old person, but splits into I and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulation is excessive admiration or flattery, the kind of worship a devoted fan gives a star.

clue.text: This writer’s going after a goal

blocks.note: taken as written
the setter refers to themself: this writer is, I'm

explanation.surface: The setter says they are chasing an objective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This writer' is the setter, so 'this writer's' is I'm, placed after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim is a purpose or target someone works towards, the same as an objective.

clue.text: Cooked a suet dish

indicators.note: cooking changes food's form, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Making a pudding with suet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' wants to be the definition, a verb like fried; the definition is the noun 'dish'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauté is a meal of food fried quickly in a little fat, so it can name a whole course.

clue.text: Old characters travel around to get meat

indicators.note: turning around means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: to go is to travel
ham is a meat

explanation.surface: Elderly folk going on a trip to buy meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old characters' looks like elderly people, but the characters are letters of an alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogham is an early medieval Irish alphabet of notches and strokes carved along the edges of stones.

clue.text: Most fond of outdoor life, stops delving into screen message

indicators.note: something delving into another digs inside it

blocks.note: a tweet is a short message posted on social media and read on a screen
an engine that stops dies

explanation.surface: A countryside lover quits searching through online posts.
explanation.walkthrough: Tweedy suggests the hearty country type in tweeds who likes fishing and shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweedy people favour country pursuits and rugged tweed clothing, so the tweediest are the keenest on outdoor living.
